summary: Mark C. Elliott works in sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He has held posts as a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and as Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University.

Mark Csikszentmihalyi is a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He served as an associate professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1994 to 2006 and became Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at UC Berkeley around 2006.

Mark D. Griffiths studied at the University of Exeter from 1987 to 1990. He held posts at the University of Plymouth (1990-1995) and Nottingham Trent University, where he became Professor of Gambling Studies around 1995.

Mark Juergensmeyer works in religious studies and indology. He studied at the University of Illinois System, Columbia University's SIPA, and Union Theological Seminary, and was appointed professor of sociology and religious studies at UC Santa Barbara around 1993.

Mark L. Blum works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held an assistant professorship at the State University of New York (attested 2005) and was an associate professor at the University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2006).
Mark Owen specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Leeds, where he was supervised by Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.
Indologist Mark S. G. Dyczkowski completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich. He also studied under traditional teachers Lakshman Joo and Kedar Raj Rajopadhyaya.

Mark Siderits is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and indology. He was on the faculty at Illinois State University from around 1979 to 2008, later serving as Emeritus Professor of Philosophy there and at Seoul National University (~2008-2014).

Indology and religious studies scholar Mark Singleton earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge and studied under Lakshmi Tatacharya. He is attested as a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London in 2020.

Mark T. Unno, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, studied at Oberlin College (~1977-1981) and Stanford University (~1987-1994). He held posts at Brown University (~1994-1998) and the University of Oregon (~1998).

Mark Tatz specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz, studied under traditional teachers including Tenzin Dragpa Chokyi Gyaltsen, and was a professor at CIIS (attested 1988).
Mark Teeuwen specializes in Japanology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Leiden University (~1991-1996) and became Professor of Japanese Studies at the University of Oslo around 1999.

Markus Viehbeck works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, and has held positions at the University of Vienna and Heidelberg University.

Marsha Weidner specializes in sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and held posts in art history at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

Philosopher Martha Nussbaum studied at New York University (~1965-1969) and Harvard University (~1969-1975). She held academic posts at Harvard (~1975-1983), Brown University (~1983-1995), and the University of Chicago (~1995).
Martin Baumann is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He joined the University of Lucerne in 2001, where he served as Professor of Religious Studies.

Martin Brauen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at the universities of Delhi and Zurich, as well as with traditional teachers. He worked as a Konservator at the University of Zurich from around 1975 to 2008.

Martin Collcutt, a historian of Japan, studied at Fitzwilliam College, Cambridge, and earned his PhD from Harvard (1969). He taught at Yokohama National University, the University of Tokyo, and served at Princeton University (1975-2015), directing its East Asian Studies Program.

Martin Delhey, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He has held research and teaching posts at Hamburg, Göttingen, Shandong University, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Ryukoku University.

Martin Haug was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübingen and Bonn under Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at Bonn, Heidelberg, Deccan College (~1859-1866), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1868-1876).
